title: Creating a Structurally Realistic Finite Element Geometric Model of a Cardiomyocyte to Study the Role of Cellular Architecture in Cardiomyocyte Systems Biology
protocol: Prepare 0.15 M sodium cacodylate buffer at pH 7.4 according to Table 1.
Prepare 0.3 M sodium cacodylate buffer at pH 7.4 according to Table 1.
Dissolve 2 g of PFA powder in 20 mL of distilled water at 60 °C with constant stirring.
Add 1 M NaOH solution until the PFA solution is clear.
Wait until the temperature drops below 40 °C, then add 10 mL of glutaraldehyde and 20 mL of 0.3 M sodium cacodylate buffer.
Add 0.2 g of tannic acid to dissolve in the fixative solution.
Store three or four 20 mL scintillation vials of fixative in fridge at 4 °C, or on ice if used on the same day.
Prepare Tyrode's solution with 20 mM BDM according to Table 1.
Construct a Langendorff apparatus inside a fume cupboard.
Clamp two 100 mL plastic syringe tubes to two different retort stands, approximately 70 cm high from the stand base.
Connect the plastic syringe tubes and a connector tube using 3 mm-inner-diameter tubing and a three-way stopcock.
Fit a 3 mm outer-diameter cannula to the bottom of the connector tubing.
Fill syringe tubes with Tyrode's solution and fixative solutions at 37 °C.
Remove air bubbles within the tubing by passing the syringe solutions through them.
Anesthetize the animal by treating the rat (200-250 g by body weight) with 0.5 mL of 250 U/mL heparin via intraperitoneal injection.
Wait for 10 min, then treat the rat with intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital (210 mg/kg of body weight).
Confirm a proper degree of anesthesia by testing the toe pinch reflex.
Euthanize the animal by cervical dislocation.
Harvest the heart using dissection procedures similar to previously published articles.
Place the heart in ice-cold saline.
Isolate the ascending aorta and cannulate.
Ensure that the tip of the cannula sits just above the semi-lunar valve.
Tie a thread tightly around the ascending aorta.
Connect the cannula to the gravity-driven Langendorff apparatus operated at ~70 cm above the base of the system.
Twist the stopcock on the Langendorff system to perfuse the heart with Tyrode's solution containing 20 mM BDM.
Twist the stopcock to begin perfusion with a fixative of 2% paraformaldehyde, 2.5% glutaraldehyde, and 0.2% tannic acid in 0.15 M sodium cacodylate at 37 °C for 10 min.
Dissect tissue blocks from the left ventricular free wall using a razor blade to obtain samples approximately 1 mm³ in size.
Store the dissected tissue blocks in pre-cooled scintillation vials containing fixative on ice for 2 h.
Cool 100 mL of 0.15 M sodium cacodylate buffer on ice.

Prepare equal volumes of 4% osmium tetroxide and 0.3 M sodium cacodylate, then add 0.08 g potassium ferrocyanide to make a heavy metal stain solution containing 2% potassium ferrocyanide in the fixative.
Cool the heavy metal stain solution on ice.
Pipette out the initial fixative from the vials and replace it with enough cold 0.15 M sodium cacodylate buffer to submerge samples.
Place the vials containing samples and buffer on ice for 5 min.
Repeat step 2.2.3 four more times with 0.15 M sodium cacodylate.
Pre-cool all solutions on ice before adding them to the sample.
Cover the sample with solution at all times during washing.
Add new solution quickly after removing previous solution.
Keep scintillation vials on ice between washes.
Replace sodium cacodylate buffer with ice-cold heavy metal stain solution.
Store the sample containing heavy metal stain solution on ice overnight.
Shake the vial by hand to ensure that ferrocyanide is well mixed.
Work in the fume hood when performing this step due to toxicity of osmium.
Dilute 4% aqueous uranyl acetate stock solution to 2% using equal volumes of stock UA and double distilled water.
Cool down the diluted uranyl acetate on ice.
Replace heavy metal stain with ice-cooled 0.15 M sodium cacodylate buffer.
Let the sample incubate for 5 min on ice after replacing heavy metal stain.
Repeat step 2.2.7 four more times on ice to rinse off excess heavy metal stain solution.
Rinse samples four times with purified water, waiting 2 minutes between each rinse.
Incubate samples in ice-cold 2% UA for 60-120 min on ice.
Cool five 20 mL scintillation vials of ethanol to different percentages (20%, 50%, 70%, 90%, and 100%) on ice.
Rinse samples in purified water four times with 2-minute intervals on ice.

Dehydrate samples by sequentially replacing the solution within the sample vial with increasing concentrations of cold ethanol for 10 minutes each: 20% ethanol, then 50%, 70%, 90%, and finally twice in 100% ethanol.
Replace the final 100% ethanol with cooled pure acetone to transition samples to room temperature.
Allow the sample vial to sit on a room-temperature lab bench for 10 minutes after replacing ethanol with acetone.
Rinse samples again in pure acetone at room temperature for 10 min to remove condensation.
Prepare acetone/resin solutions while samples are being processed.
Replace pure acetone in vials with a 50:50 mixture of pure acetone and epoxy resin.
Leave the resin-filled sample vials overnight on a rotor.
Embed samples in resin.
Replace 50:50 resin with 75% resin (25% acetone) and incubate for 3 h.
Incubate samples in 100% resin for 4 h at room temperature.
Replace the 100% resin with fresh 100% resin, leave overnight.
Place samples in oven-friendly containers with a flat base.
Gently pour fresh resin over the samples to embed them.
Polymerize the resin and samples in an oven at 60 °C for 48 h.
Re-orient resin blocks to image cells in cross-section.
Obtain 1 µm thick test sections from resin blocks using an ultramicrotome with a glass knife.
Stain the thick test sections for 20 s with 1% toluene blue and 1% borax.
Examine muscle cell orientation under a bright field microscope.
Re-orient longitudinally or obliquely oriented resin blocks to ensure cells are exposed to the glass knife for cross-section cutting.
Obtain semi-thin sections (~300 nm) of the reoriented tissue blocks using a diamond knife and transfer them onto copper grids.
Stain the thick sections with 2% UA and Sato lead.
Apply colloidal gold particles on both sides of the sections.
Obtain sets of single or dual-axis tilt series of projected images from -70 ° to +70 °.
Reconstruct the 3D image stack using IMOD software.
Execute the IMOD program "3dmod".
Enter the address of the ".rec" or ".mrc" file containing the 3D reconstructed image dataset into the entry box labeled "Image file(s):".
Select New Model under the "File" menu in the 3dmod graphical user interface.
Save the model file with an appropriate name using the "Save Model as"... menu item under "File".
Execute the following commands in a command-line window.
Extract a specific object from the model using "imodextract object modelfile outputmodelfile".
Create a mask for that object: imodmop -mask 255 outputmodelfile imagefile outputmask.mrc.
Convert the file into a tif stack: mrc2tif -s outputmask.mrc outputmask.tif.
Download and add iso2mesh to the MATLAB path from iso2mesh.sourceforge.net.
Download the source codes and data to simulate RyR clusters on the mesh from the github website https://github.com/CellSMB/RyR-simulator.
Start the CardiacCellMeshGenerator MATLAB application.
Load the different organelle component masks into MATLAB using the three push buttons on the upper left hand side of the GUI.
Open ImageJ.
Using the File | Open dialog, load the myofibrils and mitochondria tiff stacks into the program.
Initiate the image addition plugin by selecting "Process | Calculator Plus".
Select the myofibril image stack as i1.
Select the mitochondria image stack as i2.
Choose the "Add" operator.
Click "OK".
Select "Edit | Invert" to produce an image stack similar to Figure 6A.
Load the file containing the binary image stack of the gaps between myofibrils and mitochondria.
Push "Generate Mesh" on the GUI to trigger the iso2mesh command v2m with the 'cgalmesh' option.
Output three files: an .ele file, a .face file, and a .node file after mesh generation.
Mathematically map the spatially varying density of ion-channels onto the finite element mesh.
Push the button labelled Generate RyR-Simulator inputs on the GUI to trigger generateRyRsimulatorInputs.m.
Simulate RyR cluster distributions on the binary image stack of myofibrils.
Push the button labelled "Open RyR-simulator in R" to initiate the R program.
On the R-gui, select "File | Open".
Find and open the file "settings.R" within the RyR-Simulator package.
Also open the file ryr-simulator-parallel.R located in RyR-Simulator/source/.
Environments like Rstudio or a plain command line interface can be used.
Use the R64 command in a shell or command window if necessary.
Change parameters in settings.R file as detailed below.
Set Path2 to the folder address containing files listed in 5.1.2 for an experimentally acquired confocal image stack of RyR clusters and myofibrils.
Set Path4 to a folder address where the files generated in step 5.1.2 are stored.
Set Path3 to point to a folder where the user wants the simulated RyR cluster locations to be saved.
Set N to the number of RyR clusters to be simulated in the model (typically in the range of 200 to 300).
Set etol, a tolerance setting for the difference between experimentally measured spatial distribution and model simulated spatial distribution of RyR clusters.
Set numIter to limit the number of attempts that RyR-Simulator should take to find a simulated RyR cluster pattern satisfying the etol value.
Set numPatterns to the number of different RyR cluster patterns the user wants to simulate (typically, it is useful practice simulating 99 patterns for statistical confidence).
Set numCores to enable use of several CPU threads for faster parallel processing with R.
Install the snow package using the R package installer GUI.
Install the doSNOW package using the R package installer GUI.
Install the doParallel package using the R package installer GUI.
Install the foreach package using the R package installer GUI.
Install the iterators package using the R package installer GUI.
Install the rgl package using the R package installer GUI.
Execute the simulator by entering "source('path to ryr-simulator-parallel.R',chdir=TRUE)" in the R command window.
Select a simulated RyR cluster distribution text file from those output by the RyR-Simulator.
Execute "RyR Density Mapper" on the MATLAB GUI.
Map the spatial locations of the simulated RyR clusters onto the finite element mesh using the spherical kernel intensity estimator method.
